# OBS001 `common-block`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A `common` block.

## Why

Common blocks share storage by position, not by name: every program unit must repeat the same
layout, and a mismatch silently reinterprets memory. They are obsolescent since Fortran 2018. Put
the shared data in a module.

## Reported

```fortran
common /state/ t, dt
```

## Preferred

```fortran
module state
  real :: t, dt
end module state
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OBS001] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OBS001` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).
